text: Found it — the draftReply config has a stopSequences setting that stops generation at the first newline, which looks like a normal 'stop' finish reason but actually truncates output. I should remove that config and check other files like ai.ts or agents.ts for similar stopSequences usage, comparing against the greet prompt.

The likely culprit is `config: { stopSequences: ['\n'] }` in `draftReply` (line 64): a newline stop sequence would cut the reply after the first line. I'll confirm nothing else sets stop sequences, and check the other config for context.

input.command: grep -rn "stopSequences\|stop_sequences\|maxOutputTokens" src prompts; echo "---"; cat src/ai.ts; echo "---"; cat prompts/greet.prompt
input.description: Search for stop sequence settings and show ai.ts

text: I should just remove the whole config line rather than trying to preserve parts of it. The "stop" finishReason is expected here since there's a stopSequence set to '\n' on line 64, which explains why Gemini halts generation there. I've already read flows.ts, so I'm ready to make the edit now.
The only stop sequence in the app is `['\n']` on line 64, and the model-level config in `ai.ts` doesn't set one. I'll remove that config line so the reply isn't cut at the first newline.

The root cause was a newline stop sequence in `draftReply`. `src/flows.ts:64` had `config: { stopSequences: ['\n'] }`, so the model halted at the first line break. I removed that line, and the type-check passes.

I wrote `answer.json` in the project root with the file, the replaced snippet, the cause, and the evidence. I did not run the flow against the live model, so the fix is confirmed by reading the code and type-checking, not by a real reply.
